title: SGCD: Stain-Guided CycleDiffusion for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation of Histopathology Image Classification

problems.title: Target class labels determine adaptation-sample selection
problems.source_location: Introduction and Section 4.3, PDF pp.1 and 7; main.py, lines 61–84 and 129
claim: `main.py` constructs the target training `CoordDataset` with class balancing enabled; the loader obtains labels from filename prefixes before downsampling.
analysis: Changing only those target class annotations can therefore change which image identities enter adaptation, even if minibatch labels are later discarded. In the balanced-subset operation, label information has already affected the training input. An externally predeclared curator subset would be a different protocol.
result: The release is not strictly label-blind target adaptation. Accuracy advantage, patient leakage and historical split preprocessing are not established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use all eligible target training images or a selection rule independent of their class annotations. Identify any external subset manifest explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public protocol discrepancy without verified attribution to the central original results.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Target-test AUC selects saved checkpoints
problems.source_location: Section 5, PDF pp.7–9; main.py, lines 130–135 and 552–559
claim: The release repeatedly evaluates the dataset explicitly opened in testing mode and saves model components when its AUC improves.
analysis: For fixed scores \((0.1,0.9,0.6,0.7)\) and \((0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4)\), labels \((0,0,1,1)\) give AUCs \((0.5,1)\); reversing labels gives \((0.5,0)\). The selected epoch changes with test labels while predictions are fixed. This is model selection rather than logging alone.
result: The release uses test outcomes in selection. Its historical optimism or effect on reported AUC is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Select by an independently declared validation rule or prespecified epoch, then evaluate on untouched final test data. A labeled target validation set changes the supervision protocol.
problems.impact_rationale: The release selection dependence is explicit; a large original-result effect is not demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The classifier branch backpropagates without stepping its optimizer
problems.source_location: Section 4.3, Eq.(9), PDF p.7; main.py, lines 373–388 and 521–543
claim: Section 4.3 specifies classifier optimization. The classifier branch calls backward, but the only optimizer step in the surrounding loop is inside the diffusion branch.
analysis: For \(L(w)=w^2/2\) at \(w=1\), backward creates gradient \(1\) but leaves the parameter unchanged; SGD at rate \(0.1\) would give \(0.9\). The diffusion optimizer owns different parameters and cannot substitute. Batch-normalization buffers may still change.
result: The public classifier branch omits parameter optimization, not every possible change in its function.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use a persistent classifier optimizer, matching scheduler and explicit intended trainable parameter set; clear gradients, backpropagate and step in that phase.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release optimizer omission with unresolved historical experiment correspondence.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Guidance is bypassed and its dormant derivative is incomplete
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Eq.(3), PDF p.5; Algorithm 2, PDF p.15; main.py, lines 278–321
claim: The reverse function sets `guide` false internally; its dormant routine returns a normalized residual without the clean-estimator Jacobian and ignores its locally zeroed cutoff scale.
analysis: With \(A_t=1/4\), denoiser \(\epsilon(x)=2x/\sqrt3\) and reference \(1\), the clean estimate is \(2x-\sqrt3\epsilon(x)=0\). The norm of its difference from the reference is constant, so its derivative is zero. The dormant normalized residual is instead \(-1\). This occurs away from the norm’s nondifferentiable boundary.
result: The release neither applies requested guidance nor computes the stated full derivative if merely enabled.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Honor the guidance flag and cutoff, and differentiate through the declared clean-image estimator, or explicitly specify and evaluate a different approximation.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public guidance-path discrepancy; its effect on original experiments is not verified.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The custom sampler doubles variance and mismatches time indices
problems.source_location: Eq.(2), PDF p.3; Algorithm 2, PDF p.15; main.py, lines 259–274, 318–319 and 596
claim: The custom reverse step combines a deterministic direction with an unreduced additional noise variance; its loop skips ten indices while the step uses the immediate preceding index.
analysis: For a point-mass clean distribution and exact denoiser with \(A_t=0.64\), \(A_s=0.81\), the step gives \(x_s=\sqrt{0.19}\epsilon+\sqrt{0.19}z\) for independent standard normals, hence variance \(0.38\) instead of \(0.19\). A loop at times \((30,20,10,0)\) first transitions using index \(29\), then treats that output as time \(20\). The final \(T=5\) setting never reaches a clean endpoint under that stride.
result: The released kernel and time sequence are inconsistent. No full image-quality effect is measured.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Choose an actual destination \(s<t\) and a consistent DDIM variance, direction and endpoint convention. For example, use \(\sigma^2=\eta^2(1-A_s)(1-A_t/A_s)/(1-A_t)\) and direction variance \(1-A_s-\sigma^2\).
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release sampler error with no demonstrated historical benchmark attribution.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The target round trip selects the target model twice
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Eqs.(5),(7), PDF p.6; main.py, lines 499–507
claim: The claimed target-to-source-to-target cycle needs source reverse dynamics followed by target reverse dynamics; the target branch passes `model_T` to both calls.
analysis: Even deterministic inverse maps show the consequence: with \(D_S(x)=2x\), \(D_T(x)=x/2\), the intended composition sends \(1\) to \(1\); the selected double-target composition sends it to \(1/4\). The source arguments establish the selector error independently of this illustration.
result: The public route is not the stated two-domain cycle. Numerically identical models could hide the difference as a special case.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Pass the source model to the first target-cycle reverse call and the target model to reconstruction. Reconcile guidance, sampling and optimization separately.
problems.impact_rationale: This is local model routing in the later release, without established central original-result damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
